title: dev-snowflake-contract: Write summary step splices repo variables into a run: body
body:
## Plan and status

Found during the pre-open `factory-security-reviewer` pass on #58 / PR #150 (F1-S6 slice 9a). Deliberately **not** folded into that slice: a newly discovered surface stops the slice for re-scoping rather than being absorbed because it is adjacent (AGENTS.md, Rigour Calibration).

Current delivery status is owned by the [cloud state registry](https://github.com/syamaner/roastpilot-cloud/blob/main/docs/state/registry.md).

Refs #11, Refs #10.

## Context

`.github/workflows/dev-snowflake-contract.yml`'s `Write summary` step interpolates repository variables directly into the shell body of a `run:` step:

```yaml
run: |
  {
    ...
    echo "- **Role:** \`${{ vars.SNOWFLAKE_DEV_ROLE }}\`"
```

GitHub Actions expression interpolation is **textual and happens before bash parses the line**, so a variable whose value contains a command substitution is executed rather than printed. `vars.SNOWFLAKE_DEV_DATABASE` and `vars.SNOWFLAKE_DEV_WAREHOUSE` are the same shape. This was reproduced during review; the exploit string is deliberately omitted here since the repository is public.

This is the only such sink in the repository. All seven workflows were swept during the review; the other interpolations into `run:` bodies use `github.repository`, which is not attacker-controlled.

### Why it is bounded, and why it still matters

Bounded:

- setting a repository variable requires admin, and an admin can already read or replace the Environment secret directly, so this is not a privilege escalation;
- the job is `workflow_dispatch`-only behind the `dev-snowflake-ci` Environment with a required reviewer;
- by the time this step runs, the private key file has been removed by its `trap ... EXIT` and the secret env vars are scoped to earlier steps.

Still worth fixing:

- the step is `if: always()`, so it runs **after** the grant-audit steps have already refused a malformed identifier and failed. The `assert_sql_identifier_safe` guard added in #58 structurally cannot protect this sink;
- `harden-runner`'s allowlist includes `github.com:443` and `api.github.com:443`, so injected code has an egress channel;
- #58 hardened the weaker sink (identifiers reaching `SHOW` statements, where a hostile value already failed closed) while this stronger one, in the same file, was left. The reasoning used to justify the weaker one, "these variables are operator-controlled", is exactly what leaves this open.

## Acceptance contract

- No repository variable, or any other expression-interpolated value, is spliced into a `run:` shell body in `dev-snowflake-contract.yml`. Bind them through `env:` so they reach the script as shell variables and are never parsed as script text.
- The rendered job summary keeps its current content and formatting.
- A repository-wide check confirms no other workflow reintroduces the pattern.
- Preserve every existing control in this workflow: the Environment gate, `egress-policy: block`, the two grant-audit call sites, the `trap`-based key cleanup, and the timeout budget.

## Out of scope

Changing what the summary reports, the grant-audit logic, the identifier guard from #58, or any Environment/branch-protection configuration.

## Verification contract

`factory-security-reviewer` (the diff touches `.github/**`). A test asserting the `env:`-bound form, plus the offline workflow gates. No live Snowflake dispatch is required to verify this change.

## Notes

Conventional/interactive execution: the diff touches `.github/**`, which a factory implementing-agent patch may never modify.
